source_refs.note: Book p. 226-229: 7.1.6 derivation of v = u + at, x = ut + at^2/2, 2ax = v^2 - u^2 (equations (1)-(5)), Examples 7-10 (Example 10 ends at the top of p. 229)

blocks.text: Bachon, ab tak humne graphs se motion ko samjha. Ab hum woh teen mashhoor equations khud derive karenge (yani khud bana kar dekhenge ke kahan se aati hain) jo aap physics mein bhi parhte hain: \(v = u + at\), \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2}\) aur \(2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\). Physics mein yeh aksar graph se nikaali jati hain; yahan hum calculus (integration) se nikaalenge. Is ka faida yeh hai ke jab acceleration constant na ho (Example 9 aur 10), tab bhi yahi tareeqa, yani integrate karo aur initial condition se constant nikaalo, kaam aata hai. Pehle derivation, phir char misaalein.

Kitab kehti hai: constant acceleration se chalne wale particle ki motion parhne ke liye hum char quantities dekhte hain: displacement, time, velocity aur acceleration. Aam taur par in mein se kuch maloom hoti hain aur baaqi nikaalni hoti hain. In ko aapas mein jorne ke liye hum equations of motion use karte hain. Maan lijiye ek particle seedhi line mein constant acceleration \(a\) se chal raha hai. Waqt \(t = 0\) par particle point \(O\) par hai (yani \(x = 0\)) aur us ki initial (shuru wali) velocity \(u\) hai. Chun ke acceleration waqt ke lihaaz se velocity ka instantaneous rate of change (lamhati tabdeeli ki sharah) hai, is liye:
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = a \Rightarrow dv = a\,dt\]
Dono taraf integrate karne se:
\[\int dv = \int a\,dt\]
\[v = at + c \quad \text{...(1)}\]
(jahan \(c\) constant of integration hai)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Hum integrate kyun kar rahe hain? \(\frac{dv}{dt} = a\) humein velocity ka rate batata hai, velocity khud nahin. Rate se asal cheez wapas lane ka amal integration hai, bilkul jaise kisi tanki mein paani aane ki raftaar se kul paani nikaalna. Chun ke \(a\) constant hai, \(\int a\,dt = at\). Lekin har indefinite integral ke saath ek constant \(c\) aata hai, kyun ke kisi constant ka derivative zero hota hai. Yeh \(c\) kya hai, yeh "initial condition" (shuru ki halat) batati hai.

Initial condition \(v = u\) at \(t = 0\) ko equation (1) mein rakhein:
\[u = 0 + c \Rightarrow c = u\]
Wapas equation (1) mein rakhne se:
\[v = u + at \quad \text{...(2)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Dekha aap ne? Constant \(c\) koi ajeeb cheez nahin, yeh shuru wali velocity \(u\) hi hai. Equation (2) ka matlab bhi aasan hai: aakhri velocity = shuru ki velocity + (har second barhne wali velocity \(\times\) kitne second). Maslan \(u = 4\) m/s aur \(a = 2\) m/s\(^2\) ho to 3 second baad \(v = 4 + 2 \times 3 = 10\) m/s.

Ab velocity waqt ke lihaaz se displacement ka instantaneous rate of change hai:
\[v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}\]
\[\Rightarrow \dfrac{dx}{dt} = u + at\]
\[\Rightarrow dx = (u + at)\,dt\]
Dono taraf integrate karne se:
\[\int dx = \int (u + at)\,dt\]
\[x = ut + a\dfrac{t^{2}}{2} + c_{1} \quad \text{...(3)}\]
Initial condition \(x = 0\) at \(t = 0\) ko equation (3) mein rakhein:
\[0 = 0 + 0 + c_{1} \Rightarrow c_{1} = 0\]
Wapas equation (3) mein rakhne se:
\[x = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2} \quad \text{...(4)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yahan \(u\) aur \(a\) dono constants hain, is liye \(\int u\,dt = ut\) aur \(\int at\,dt = a\frac{t^{2}}{2}\) (power rule: power ek barhao aur nayi power se taqseem karo). \(c_{1} = 0\) is liye aaya kyun ke humne shuru wali jagah \(O\) ko hi zero maana tha. Agar particle kisi aur jagah \(x_{0}\) se chalta to \(c_{1} = x_{0}\) aata.

Ab equation (2) se:
\[t = \dfrac{v - u}{a}\]
Ise equation (4) mein rakh kar \(t\) ko khatam karte hain:
\[x = u\left(\dfrac{v - u}{a}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}a\left(\dfrac{v - u}{a}\right)^{2}\]
Simplify karne se:
\[2ax = v^{2} - u^{2} \quad \text{...(5)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab "By simplification" keh kar yeh qadam chhod deti hai. Aayiye poora karte hain. Doosre term mein \(a\) ek baar cancel hota hai, phir common denominator \(2a\) lete hain aur \((v - u)\) common nikaalte hain:
\[x = \dfrac{u(v - u)}{a} + \dfrac{(v - u)^{2}}{2a}\]
\[= \dfrac{2u(v - u) + (v - u)^{2}}{2a}\]
\[= \dfrac{(v - u)(2u + v - u)}{2a}\]
\[= \dfrac{(v - u)(v + u)}{2a}\]
\[= \dfrac{v^{2} - u^{2}}{2a}\]
\[\Rightarrow 2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\]
Aakhri qadam mein \((v - u)(v + u) = v^{2} - u^{2}\) wala formula (difference of squares) laga.
Constant acceleration se chalne wale particle ki teen equations of motion yeh hain:

blocks.text_alt: v equals u plus a t
x equals u t plus one half a t squared
2 a x equals v squared minus u squared

blocks.text: Yeh equations constant acceleration wale particle ki motion ko bayan aur analyse karne ke liye bohat zyada use hoti hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sab se ahem sawal: kaun si equation kab? Har equation mein char cheezein hain aur paanchvi ghaib hai. Sawal mein dekhiye ke \(u, v, a, x, t\) mein se kaun si cheez na di gayi hai na poochi gayi; wahi equation chuniye jis mein woh cheez nahin. Neeche ki table yahi batati hai.
Dhyan dein: yeh teeno equations sirf tab sahi hain jab acceleration constant ho. Agar \(a\) waqt ke saath badle (jaise \(a = t^{2} + \cos t\)), to inhein mat lagaiye; wahan seedha integrate karna parta hai, jaise Example 9 aur 10 mein.

header: Is mein kaun si cheez nahin
rows: jab \(x\) na diya ho na poocha ho
jab \(v\) na diya ho na poocha ho
jab \(t\) na diya ho na poocha ho
blocks.caption: Equation of motion chunne ka tareeqa (hamari taraf se, kitab mein nahin)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: In equations ka graph se bhi rishta samajh lijiye, jo 7.1.5 mein parha tha. Constant acceleration ka velocity-time graph ek seedhi line hai jo \(u\) se shuru ho kar \(t\) second baad \(v\) tak pohanchti hai. Is line ka slope \(\frac{v - u}{t} = a\) hai, aur yahi \(v = u + at\) hai. Is line ke neeche ka area ek trapezium hai jis ki parallel sides \(u\) aur \(v\) aur height \(t\) hai: area \(= \frac{1}{2}(u + v)t\). Is mein \(v = u + at\) rakhein to \(ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2}\) aata hai, yani wahi equation (4). Matlab calculus aur graph dono ek hi nateeja dete hain; aap jo tareeqa aasan lage, us se samajh sakte hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh misaal hamari taraf se hai.) Ek scooter 4 m/s se chal raha hai aur 2 m/s\(^2\) se yaksaan raftaar pakadta hai. 3 second baad us ki velocity aur is dauran tay kiya gaya faasla?
\[v = 4 + 2 \times 3 = 10 \text{ m/s}\]
\[x = 4 \times 3 + \tfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 3^{2} = 21 \text{ m}\]
Tasdeeq teesri equation se: \(2 \times 2 \times 21 = 84\) aur \(10^{2} - 4^{2} = 100 - 16 = 84\). Dono barabar, matlab jawab sahi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab misaalon se pehle ek pakka tareeqa (routine) bana lete hain jo har sawal mein kaam aayega:
Pehla qadam: sawal parh kar paanch cheezon ki list banao: \(u\), \(v\), \(a\), \(x\), \(t\). Jo diya hai us ke aage value likho, jo poocha hai us ke aage sawaliya nishaan.
Doosra qadam: chhupi hui values pehchaano. "Starts from rest" ka matlab \(u = 0\); "comes to rest" ya "stops" ka matlab \(v = 0\); "highest point" par bhi \(v = 0\).
Teesra qadam: dekho kaun si cheez na di gayi na poochi gayi; wahi equation lo jis mein woh nahin.
Chautha qadam: units ek jaisi karo (km/h ko m/s mein badalna ho to 1000 se zarb aur 3600 se taqseem).
Paanchvan qadam: jawab nikaal kar kisi doosri equation se tasdeeq karo.
Yeh routine aap ko ghalat equation chunne se bachayegi, jo is topic ki sab se aam ghalti hai.

blocks.title: Example 7
blocks.problem: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 3 m/s\(^2\). Find the velocity of the car after 5 seconds.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(u = 0\) (car rest se chalti hai), \(a = 3\) m/s\(^2\), \(t = 5\) s.
Maloom karna: \(v\).
Tareeqa: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke kya diya hai aur kya chahiye: \(u, a, t\) diye hain, \(v\) chahiye. Displacement \(x\) na diya hai na poocha, is liye woh equation chuniye jis mein \(x\) nahin: \(v = u + at\).

Equation mein values rakhein
\[v = u + at\]
\[v = 0 + 3 \times 5\]
\[= 15 \text{ m/s}\]
Kyun: "rest se chalna" ka matlab hai shuru mein velocity zero, yani \(u = 0\). Har second velocity 3 m/s barhti hai, to 5 second mein 15 m/s.
Dhyan dein: "starts from rest" ko hamesha \(u = 0\) mein badlein; yeh aksar sawal mein lafzon mein chhupa hota hai.

Tasdeeq:
Faasla \(x = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(3)(5^{2}) = 37.5\) m. Teesri equation: \(2ax = 2 \times 3 \times 37.5 = 225\) aur \(v^{2} - u^{2} = 15^{2} - 0 = 225\). Barabar hain.
Andaaze se bhi dekhiye: 15 m/s taqreeban 54 km/h banta hai (15 ko 3.6 se zarb). Ek aam car ke liye 5 second mein rest se 54 km/h tak pohanchna bilkul mumkin hai, to jawab haqeeqat ke qareeb bhi hai. Jawab ko is tarah "kya yeh mumkin hai?" wale sawal se parakhna achhi aadat hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "(car stats from vert)" chhapa hai aur \(a = 3\) m/s\(^2\) ke baad comma ghaib hai. Sahi ibarat hai: "\(u = 0\) (car starts from rest), \(a = 3\) m/s\(^2\), \(t = 5\) s". Hal aur jawab 15 m/s bilkul theek hain.

blocks.title: Example 8
blocks.problem: A car accelerates from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 seconds. Find the distance covered during this time.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(u = 10\) m/s, \(v = 30\) m/s, \(t = 4\) s.
Maloom karna: is dauran tay kiya gaya faasla \(x\).
Tareeqa: \(x\) ke liye har equation mein \(a\) chahiye, jo diya nahin. To pehle \(v = u + at\) se \(a\) nikaalenge (is mein \(x\) nahin), phir \(2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\) se \(x\).

Pehle acceleration
\[v = u + at\]
\[30 = 10 + a \times 4\]
\[\Rightarrow 4a = 20\]
\[\Rightarrow a = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5 \text{ m/s}^{2}\]
Kyun: dono taraf se 10 minus kiya to \(4a = 20\), phir 4 se taqseem. Velocity 4 second mein 20 m/s barhi, yani har second 5 m/s.

Ab faasla
\[2ax = v^{2} - u^{2} \quad \text{...(1)}\]
\[2 \times 5x = 30^{2} - 10^{2} = 800\]
\[\Rightarrow x = \dfrac{800}{10} = 80 \text{ meter}\]
Kyun: \(u, v, a\) ab maloom hain aur \(x\) chahiye; is equation mein \(t\) ki zaroorat nahin. \(30^{2} - 10^{2} = 900 - 100 = 800\).
Dhyan dein: \(30^{2} - 10^{2}\) ko \((30 - 10)^{2} = 400\) mat likhiye; pehle square karein phir minus.

Tasdeeq:
Doosri equation se: \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2} = 10 \times 4 + \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 16 = 40 + 40 = 80\) m. Wahi jawab.
Ek aur aasan tareeqa: constant acceleration mein average velocity \(\frac{10 + 30}{2} = 20\) m/s, aur \(20 \times 4 = 80\) m.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein Example 8 ke qadam aage peeche chhap gaye hain: \(30 = 10 + a \times 4\) ke foran baad equation (1) \(2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\) likh di gayi hai, aur phir \(4a = 20\) aata hai. Halaan ke \(4a = 20\) pehli equation \(30 = 10 + 4a\) se nikalta hai, (1) se nahin. Sahi tarteeb: pehle \(a = 5\) m/s\(^2\) poora karein, phir (1) se \(x\) nikaalein. Jawab \(a = 5\) m/s\(^2\) aur \(x = 80\) m theek hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Example 8 wali car agar 30 m/s se yaksaan dheemi ho kar 6 second mein ruk jaye, to brake lagne ke baad kitna faasla tay karegi?
Jawab: \(u = 30\), \(v = 0\), \(t = 6\). Yahan \(a\) maloom nahin aur \(x\) poocha hai. Pehle \(0 = 30 + 6a\) se \(a = -5\) m/s\(^2\) (minus, kyun ke raftaar kam ho rahi hai). Phir \(2(-5)x = 0 - 900\), yani \(x = 90\) m. Isi liye sarkon par tez raftaar khatarnak hai: rukne ka faasla raftaar ke square ke hisaab se barhta hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh misaal hamari taraf se hai, badalte acceleration ki tayyari ke liye.) Ek particle \(t = 0\) par origin se rest se chalta hai aur us ka acceleration \(a(t) = 6t\) hai. \(v(t)\) aur \(x(t)\)?
\[v = \int 6t\,dt = 3t^{2} + c,\quad v(0) = 0 \Rightarrow c = 0\]
\[x = \int 3t^{2}\,dt = t^{3} + c_{1},\quad x(0) = 0 \Rightarrow c_{1} = 0\]
To \(v = 3t^{2}\) aur \(x = t^{3}\). Agar koi ghalti se \(v = u + at\) lagata to \(v = 0 + 6t \cdot t = 6t^{2}\) aata, jo ghalat hai (derivative \(12t\) banta hai, \(6t\) nahin). Yahi wajah hai ke badalte acceleration mein sirf integration chalegi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Ab ek bari tabdeeli aa rahi hai. Example 9 aur 10 mein acceleration constant nahin, balke waqt ke saath badalta hai. Is liye wahan \(v = u + at\) jaisi equations bilkul nahin lagengi. Wahan wahi kaam karenge jo derivation mein kiya tha: \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\) ko integrate kar ke \(v\), phir \(v = \frac{dx}{dt}\) ko integrate kar ke \(x\), aur har baar initial condition se constant nikaalna. Yaad rakhiye: \(\int \cos t\,dt = \sin t\) aur \(\int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t\).

blocks.title: Example 9
blocks.problem: Find the position and the velocity of a particle moving along a straight line at any time \(t\) seconds, given that starts from rest at \(t = 0\) and is subject to an acceleration \(a(t) = t^{2} + \cos t\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(a(t) = t^{2} + \cos t\); particle \(t = 0\) par rest se chalta hai, yani \(v(0) = 0\). Kitab position ke liye bhi shuru wali jagah ko origin maanti hai: \(x(0) = 0\).
Maloom karna: kisi bhi waqt \(t\) par velocity \(v(t)\) aur position \(x(t)\).
Tareeqa: acceleration constant nahin, is liye equations of motion nahin lag sakti. Do baar integrate karenge: pehle \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\) se \(v\), phir \(v = \frac{dx}{dt}\) se \(x\).

Acceleration ko integrate karein
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = t^{2} + \cos t\]
\[\Rightarrow dv = (t^{2} + \cos t)\,dt\]
\[\Rightarrow \int dv = \int (t^{2} + \cos t)\,dt\]
\[v(t) = \dfrac{1}{3}t^{3} + \sin t + c\]
Kyun: \(\because\ a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt}\). Power rule se \(\int t^{2}\,dt = \frac{t^{3}}{3}\), aur \(\int \cos t\,dt = \sin t\).

Initial condition \(v = 0\) at \(t = 0\)
\[0 = 0 + 0 + c \Rightarrow c = 0\]
\[v(t) = \dfrac{1}{3}t^{3} + \sin t\]
Kyun: \(\sin 0 = 0\), is liye yahan constant zero aaya.

Velocity ko integrate karein
\[\dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{3}t^{3} + \sin t\]
\[\Rightarrow \int dx = \int \left(\dfrac{1}{3}t^{3} + \sin t\right)dt\]
\[x(t) = \dfrac{1}{12}t^{4} - \cos t + c_{1}\]
Kyun: yahan wajah \(\because\ v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt}\) hai (kitab is box mein ghalti se \(a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt}\) chhaapti hai). \(\int \frac{1}{3}t^{3}\,dt = \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{t^{4}}{4} = \frac{t^{4}}{12}\) aur \(\int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t\).

Initial condition \(x = 0\) at \(t = 0\)
\[0 = 0 - 1 + c_{1} \Rightarrow c_{1} = 1\]
\[x(t) = \dfrac{1}{12}t^{4} - \cos t + 1\]
Kyun: \(\cos 0 = 1\), is liye \(-\cos 0 = -1\) aata hai aur \(c_{1} = 1\) banta hai.
Dhyan dein: bohat se students yahan bhi \(c_{1} = 0\) likh dete hain kyun ke pichli dafa zero aaya tha. Har constant ko alag se nikaaliye.

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\tfrac{1}{12}t^{4} - \cos t + 1\right) = \tfrac{1}{3}t^{3} + \sin t\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\tfrac{1}{3}t^{3} + \sin t\right) = t^{2} + \cos t\]
Aur \(v(0) = 0\), \(x(0) = 0 - 1 + 1 = 0\). Sab sharait poori hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 9 mein teen chhapai ki ghaltiyan hain:
1. Sawal mein "given that starts from rest" likha hai; sahi "given that it starts from rest" hai.
2. \(\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{1}{3}t^{3} + \sin t\) ke saath wale doosre box mein \(\because a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt}\) chhapa hai. Yeh qadam velocity se position nikaal raha hai, is liye wajah \(\because v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt}\) honi chahiye.
3. \(0 = 0 - 1 + c_{1}\) se pehle wali line "Example 9 \(= 0\) at \(t = 0\):" chhapi hai, yani example ka label ghalti se dobara aa gaya. Sahi line hai: "Using the initial condition \(x = 0\) at \(t = 0\):". Yeh koi naya example nahin.
Jawab \(v(t) = \frac{1}{3}t^{3} + \sin t\) aur \(x(t) = \frac{1}{12}t^{4} - \cos t + 1\) bilkul sahi hain.

blocks.title: Example 10
blocks.problem: The acceleration (in m/s\(^2\)) of a particle is given by \(a(t) = \cos t + \sin t\). Given that the velocity is 2 m/s at \(t = 0\), find the expression for velocity \(v(t)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(a(t) = \cos t + \sin t\) (m/s\(^2\) mein), aur \(t = 0\) par \(v = 2\) m/s.
Maloom karna: velocity ka expression \(v(t)\).
Tareeqa: acceleration waqt ke saath badal raha hai, is liye \(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\) ko ek baar integrate karenge aur \(v(0) = 2\) se constant nikaalenge.

Integrate karein
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = \cos t + \sin t\]
\[\Rightarrow \int dv = \int (\cos t + \sin t)\,dt\]
\[v(t) = \sin t - \cos t + c\]
Kyun: \(\because\ a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt}\). \(\int \cos t\,dt = \sin t\) aur \(\int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t\).
Dhyan dein: \(\sin t\) ka integral \(+\cos t\) nahin, \(-\cos t\) hai, kyun ke \(\frac{d}{dt}(-\cos t) = \sin t\).

Initial condition \(v = 2\) at \(t = 0\)
\[2 = 0 - 1 + c \Rightarrow c = 3\]
\[v(t) = \sin t - \cos t + 3\]
Kyun: \(\sin 0 = 0\) aur \(\cos 0 = 1\), to \(2 = -1 + c\), yani \(c = 3\).

Tasdeeq:
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}(\sin t - \cos t + 3) = \cos t + \sin t\]
Yeh diya gaya acceleration hai. Aur \(v(0) = 0 - 1 + 3 = 2\) m/s. Dono sharait poori.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Example 10 mein agar \(t = 0\) par velocity 2 ke bajaye 0 hoti, to \(v(t)\) kya hota?
Jawab: \(0 = 0 - 1 + c\), to \(c = 1\) aur \(v(t) = \sin t - \cos t + 1\). Dekhiye, sirf constant badla; baaqi expression wahi raha. Initial condition ka kaam sirf constant tay karna hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Teen equations of motion: \(v = u + at\), \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2}\), \(2ax = v^{2} - u^{2}\); yeh \(\frac{dv}{dt} = a\) ko integrate kar ke nikalti hain.
2. Yeh sirf constant acceleration ke liye hain.
3. Equation chunne ka tareeqa: jo quantity na di gayi ho na poochi gayi ho, woh jis equation mein na ho, wahi lagaiye.
4. "Starts from rest" ka matlab \(u = 0\).
5. Acceleration waqt ke saath badle to integrate karein: \(v = \int a\,dt\), \(x = \int v\,dt\), aur har constant initial condition se nikaalein.
6. \(\int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t\), aur \(\cos 0 = 1\) (is liye constant aksar zero nahin aata).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Badalte acceleration (jaise \(t^{2} + \cos t\)) par \(v = u + at\) laga dena.
2. Constant of integration likhna bhool jana, ya baghair hisaab ke use zero maan lena.
3. \(\int \sin t\,dt\) ko \(+\cos t\) likhna.
4. \(30^{2} - 10^{2}\) ko \((30 - 10)^{2}\) samajhna.
5. Units mix karna: km/h ko m/s mein badle baghair m/s\(^2\) ke saath lagana.
6. \(a\) maloom kiye baghair seedha \(x\) wali equation mein kood jana (Example 8 mein pehle \(a\) chahiye).
